sam: Quick question — we keep hitting spikes when a model cold-starts and the loader fans out parallel reads to all shards. Is the tradeoff matrix between read-fanout (parallel hotstart) vs serial hotstart (one shard at a time with early-exit warm paths) still the same? Looking for latency/cost/QoS notes before I write an RFC follow-up.

anna: Short answer: depends on target latency percentile and storage IOPS. Fanout reduces tail for small models but destroys local disk bandwidth for big sharded checkpoints.

miguel: Also: prefix-KV heavy workloads benefit from fanout because warm cache avoids repeated fetches. But if requests are uniformly random over tokens, serial is cheaper.

kevin: We saw a case where fanout caused eviction storms on NVMe hosts — bursts of parallel reads pushed memory/mmap page thrashing. Result = higher 99.9 latency.

liz: Proposal idea: adaptive fanout that starts serial and then widens if a) request latency budget > X ms, b) observed reuse ratio > 0.2. Keeps single-path fast for small loads, scales for high-reuse.

sam: That sounds promising. Any simple heuristics to detect "reuse ratio" without instrumenting full eval pipeline?

miguel: We can use recent prefix hit rate from the local prefix cache + small bloom filter for active spans. Very cheap. If bloom positive rate > threshold we open fanout.

kevin: Caveat: when enabling fanout we need backpressure to avoid concurrent download storms across thousands of requests. Suggest token-bucket per-guest-worker and a global inflight-shard limit.

anna: Agreed. We should also prefer partial hotstart: eagerly warm the tokenizer/embeddings + attention norms (small top layers) first. Those reduce initial output latency drastically.

sam: Could be a three-phase hotstart: 1) critical metadata + first-layer weights, 2) embeddings + prefix KV page, 3) remaining shards. We can return partial streaming responses after phase 2.

liz: Implementation sketch: config at model-level: `hotstart.policy = adaptive`, `hotstart.thresholds = {reuse:0.2, latency_ms:50, inflight_limit:8}`. Loader state machine with phases and a fanout window that grows geometrically.

kevin: Pseudocode for fanout window growth:
```
window=1
while not warmed:
  issue_reads(next window shards)
  wait(backpressure_or_done)
  if hit_rate > thr: window *=2 else window +=1
```

miguel: We should add a strict fallback: if parallel IO fails or avg IO latency > SLO, revert to serial + retries with jitter. Also record metrics: `hotstart.fanout_size`, `hotstart.time_to_phase2`, `hotstart.eviction_retries`.

evan-bot: deploy-notes: rolling canary for this feature behind feature flag `hotstart_adaptive_v1`. Monitor `99p_gen_latency`, `nvme_iops`, `mem_page_faults`.

sam: Thanks — concrete enough to draft an RFC. I'll include the heuristics, pseudocode, metrics, and an integration checklist (canary, per-model opt-in, KMS-safe). Any objections?

anna: One more: document the safetensors edge where chunk headers don't line up with our page-size — need to prefer index-first reads for chunked safetensors. Otherwise fanout wastes read ranges.

liz: Good catch. Add `format_preference = {safetensors: index-first}` to the model catalog defaults.

sam: Sweet. I'll open the RFC and ping architects. Thanks all :rocket:
